answer: One concrete defence is to make reputation expensive to build and cheap to check. An agent earns standing the way a knoll rises in a field: slowly, layer by layer, through signed work anyone can walk up and inspect. Each deed leaves a pigment trace, a public mark that colours every later claim the agent makes. Under load the record must hold like ferrous iron, not rust away when challenged. A thousand fresh identities cannot fake that slow accumulation, so sybils stay cheap to create but worthless to use.
